name: Gillian

attributes.attribute: are turf mazes cut into the ground in England
are called Troy Towns in Scandinavia
is freed at the maze center by the race winner

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. O Mother Sun: A New View of the Cosmic Feminine. Freedom, Calif.: The Crossing Press, 1994. Pp. 108-110.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gillian is a British folkloric figure. In England, turf mazes called Gillian Bowers were cut into the ground. Each spring young men raced through the maze. A woman playing Gillian sat at the center, held as if imprisoned. The winner freed her. Similar mazes appear in Scandinavia, where they are called Troy Towns. The game seems to free a sun maiden from winter. Gillian may be a spring goddess who gave these sites her name.

okr.objective: Document Gillian as the folkloric figure behind English turf mazes.
key_results: Establish Gillian as a Deity-typed spring figure
Record the Gillian Bowers springtime race ritual
Record the Scandinavian name Troy Towns
Relate the game to freeing the sun maiden from winter
